summary: Resamples line strips without changing their shape, using divisions per strip, distance between points, curvature-based spacing, or points-as-keyframes along an independent variable attribute.

key_params.name: resampledivs
key_params.note: Number of divisions for per-line-strip resampling

key_params.name: resamplemindist
key_params.note: Minimum point spacing for curvature-based resampling

key_params.name: resamplemaxdist
key_params.note: Maximum point spacing for curvature-based resampling

key_params.name: resampleminmaxbias
key_params.note: Bias between min and max curvature spacing

key_params.name: usectrlpoints
key_params.note: Include exact control points from an attribute

key_params.name: ctrlpointsattr
key_params.note: Attribute identifying control points to preserve exactly

key_params.name: maxtries
key_params.note: Iteration limit used by adaptive resampling methods

key_params.name: rmvunusedpts
key_params.note: Remove points no longer referenced by output primitives

key_concepts: Line Resample changes point density while preserving the input line-strip shape, unlike Line Smooth which changes attribute values.
Resampling modes cover fixed divisions, distance spacing, curvature-adaptive spacing, and points-as-keyframes along an independent variable.
Control point, max vertex, max tries, and remove-unused-points controls keep anchors exact while bounding adaptive output size.
common_gotchas: Line Resample preserves shape; use Line Smooth when the goal is to actually smooth or relax the curve.
maxverts must be high enough for the generated vertices or output will be truncated.
ControlPoint attributes are useful for keeping anchor points exact while still resampling intermediate spans.
